reasons: Composio's Shopify toolkit page says Composio-managed OAuth is not available, so every Shopify connection runs on an app you register yourself.

On Shopify the app itself decides who can connect. An app with custom distribution installs on one store (or the stores of one Plus organization) only. To let many merchants connect, Shopify says you must publish the app through the Shopify App Store, which means a human review of your app, your listing and your data handling.
Rate limits are not a reason here: Shopify gives every app and store pair its own bucket, so one merchant's traffic never eats into another's.

verdict.summary: Your distribution choice decides everything, and you cannot change it later. One merchant's store: no review, same day. Many merchants: Shopify App Store review (about 30 days in 2026) plus a customer-data review, and App Store rules that Composio's default connect flow does not meet as-is.

timeToProduction.label: Custom distribution, one store: same day. Public, many merchants: 2-10 weeks (build to App Store rules, then a review queue Shopify staff put at about 30 days in 2026)

verdict.mainBlocker: Shopify App Store review, which any app that serves many merchants must pass, together with its protected customer data review and the rule that installation must start on Shopify, never from a form asking for the store's myshopify.com address.

stages.name: Decide the distribution method first

duration.label: 5-15 min to decide; the choice is permanent

limits: You can't change an app's distribution method after you select it.
Custom distribution: one store, or several stores in the same Plus organization. No review.
Public distribution: any number of stores, but only through the Shopify App Store (fully visible or limited visibility), and only after review.

steps.title: Pick the path that matches who will connect
steps.detail: If your agent serves one known merchant (or one Plus organization), choose custom distribution: no review, same day. If any merchant should be able to connect, you need public distribution. Shopify says apps distributed to multiple merchants must be published through the Shopify App Store. A limited-visibility listing hides the app from search, but it goes through the same requirements and the same review queue as a fully visible one.
steps.humanReason: A business decision that can't be undone on that app.

steps.title: Keep a separate development app
steps.detail: Shopify says to select the distribution method on the production app when you have separate apps for development and production. Use a second app for testing on development stores, so the permanent choice is only made once, on the app your merchants will see.

stages.name: Register the app
limits: Only apps that belong to a Partner organization get the Distribution card. An app created inside a store's own organization can only be installed on that organization's stores.
Merchant-created custom apps in the Shopify admin can no longer be created. New apps come from the Dev Dashboard or Shopify CLI.

steps.title: Create a Partner organization and a development store
steps.detail: Sign up for the Shopify Partner Program (reported as free) so the app belongs to a Partner organization; otherwise you can't distribute it to anyone else's store. Create a development store to test on: apps installed only on development stores need no protected customer data review.
steps.humanReason: Account sign-up and acceptance of the Partner Program Agreement.

steps.title: Create the app and its first version
steps.detail: In the Dev Dashboard choose Create app, name it after your product, then create a version: set the App URL, the scopes, and the redirect URL, and choose Release. Shopify recommends Shopify CLI instead of the Dev Dashboard if you plan to go on the App Store, because App Store apps need an embedded UI. Don't add scopes marked 'Shopify approval required' (such as read_all_orders) before Shopify approves them: releasing the version fails with an app_access validation error.
steps.humanReason: Requires signing in to your Shopify Partner account.

links.label: Create apps using the Dev Dashboard

preparedValues.label: Add if your agent needs them
App URL for a non-embedded test app

steps.title: Set the redirect URL
steps.detail: Paste Composio's redirect URI into the version's redirect URL field. Copy it from your Composio dashboard when you create the Shopify auth config. Shopify requires an exact match, and Composio's own knowledge base warns that older v1 and v3 callback paths can fail, while its Shopify setup article still shows a /api/v3/ path.

preparedValues.label: Redirect URL
preparedValues.value: Copy from Composio: Auth Configs > Create Auth Config > Shopify > OAuth2 > Use your own developer credentials

steps.title: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret
steps.detail: Open the app's Settings and copy the Client ID and Client Secret. The secret goes into Composio and nowhere else. A wrong secret is the most common cause of a 400 error during connection.
steps.humanReason: The secret should only pass from your dashboard to Composio.

stages.name: Connect it in Composio and test
limits: Order scopes only return orders from the last 60 days unless Shopify approves read_all_orders.
Rate limit per app and store, by the store's plan: 100 points/second (Standard), 200 (Advanced), 1,000 (Plus), 2,000 (Commerce Components).

steps.title: Create the Shopify auth config in Composio
steps.detail: Create an OAuth2 auth config for Shopify, tick 'Use your own developer credentials', and paste the Client ID and Client Secret. Use the same scopes you set in the app version. Composio's KB says not to use the old Admin API key mode for new Shopify apps. Composio also offers S2S (client credentials), but Shopify only allows that when the app and the store belong to the same organization, so it can't serve merchants' stores.

steps.title: Connect your development store
steps.detail: Start a connection and enter only the store name as the subdomain (for example your-store-name, not your-store-name.myshopify.com). Approve the install screen, then run one read tool, such as listing orders, to confirm it works. Check that the token keeps working after an hour: new public apps get offline tokens that expire every hour and must be refreshed.
steps.humanReason: You approve the install screen with your own store account.

stages.name: Path A: custom distribution to one merchant
limits: One store, or several stores in one Plus organization. Every other merchant needs a different app.
You can't charge through Shopify's app billing system.
Protected customer data (names, emails, addresses, phones) is always available to custom apps, with no review.

steps.title: Select custom distribution and send the install link
steps.detail: On the app's Home in the Dev Dashboard, open the Distribution card, choose Custom distribution, enter the merchant's myshopify.com or admin.shopify.com domain, and generate the install link. Leave 'Allow multi-store installs for one Plus organization' on if the merchant is on Plus and wants several stores. Send the link to the store owner.
steps.humanReason: A permanent choice made in your signed-in dashboard.

steps.title: Merchant installs, then connects through Composio
steps.detail: The person installing needs the 'Manage and install apps and channels' permission on the store. After install, start the Composio connection with the merchant's store name as the subdomain.
steps.humanReason: The merchant approves the install in their own store.

stages.name: Path B: public distribution, build to App Store rules

duration.label: Estimate: 1-3 weeks of engineering, depending on what you already have

limits: Installation must start on a Shopify surface; your app must not ask merchants to type their store address.
The app needs a merchant-facing UI inside the Shopify admin (App Bridge).
New public apps must use only the GraphQL Admin API.
If you charge merchants, you must bill through Shopify App Pricing or the Billing API. You keep 100% of the first $1M lifetime revenue, 85% after, plus a 2.9% processing fee.

steps.title: Replace the store-name prompt with a Shopify-initiated install
steps.detail: Composio's connect flow asks for the store subdomain. App Store requirement 2.3.1 forbids asking the merchant for it, and a Shopify staff member said in January 2026 that this applies to listed and unlisted public apps alike. Merchants must install from your App Store listing; your App URL then has to start OAuth immediately, using the shop Shopify passes to it, and send the merchant to your app's UI after they approve. Check with Composio how to pass the subdomain through its API so the merchant never types it.

steps.title: Build the embedded admin UI
steps.detail: Every App Store app must be usable through a UI and give a consistent embedded experience in the Shopify admin with the latest App Bridge. Embedded apps must work without third-party cookies. For an agent product this is usually a settings and activity page that runs inside the admin.

steps.title: Host the three mandatory compliance webhooks
steps.detail: Subscribe to customers/data_request, customers/redact and shop/redact, accept JSON POSTs, and return 401 for an invalid HMAC. Apps without them are rejected. These endpoints live on your server, not Composio's.

steps.title: Confirm expiring tokens and GraphQL-only calls
steps.detail: New public apps can't use non-expiring offline tokens for the GraphQL Admin API: the code exchange must send expiring=1, and the 1-hour token must be refreshed with a refresh token that lasts up to 90 days. Composio says it handles refresh for custom credentials; confirm it requests expiring tokens for your app. Also use only Composio's GraphQL tools, since its toolkit still carries legacy REST actions and new public apps must be GraphQL-only.

steps.title: Move billing onto Shopify, if you charge merchants
steps.detail: Apps with off-platform billing can't be distributed through the App Store. If merchants pay you for the agent, the charge must go through Shopify App Pricing or the Billing API, and plan changes must work without contacting support.
steps.humanReason: A pricing and revenue decision for your company.

stages.name: Path B: public distribution, Shopify review

duration.label: No published SLA. Shopify staff said ~30 days in 2026; recent reports range from 16 days to over 2 months

limits: Resubmitting puts you at the back of the queue; reply to the reviewer instead.
Repeatedly failing review can suspend your submission for a set period.
You can't apply for protected customer data while the app is under review.

steps.title: Request protected customer data and gated scopes before you submit
steps.detail: Order and customer data is protected customer data. In the Partner Dashboard, open API access requests, request protected customer data and each field you need (name, email, phone, address), give your reasons, and complete the data protection details. Level 2 (any of those four fields) means meeting extra security controls: encrypted backups, separate test and production data, a data loss prevention strategy, limited staff access, strong passwords and access logs. Request read_all_orders here too if your agent needs orders older than 60 days. Ask only for what the agent uses: Shopify approves the minimum, and unapproved fields come back as null.
steps.humanReason: Declarations about how your company handles merchant and customer data.

steps.title: Register, list and submit
steps.detail: Pay the one-time $19 App Store registration fee, select public distribution, and complete the App Store review page: app URLs (no 'Shopify' or 'Example' in the domain), compliance webhooks, a 1200 x 1200 icon, an emergency contact, and at least one listing. Run the automated checks until they pass, then submit. Write clear test instructions; one September 2026 review was held up by a request for a screencast.
steps.humanReason: A payment and a submission on behalf of your company.

steps.title: Answer the reviewer, don't resubmit
steps.detail: The app moves from Submitted to Paused (core requirements missing) or Reviewed (fixes to discuss) before Published. Reply to the reviewer's email or submit fixes from the status banner. A Shopify staff member said in October 2026 that submitted fixes go back into the general queue.
steps.humanReason: Correspondence with Shopify's review team, sometimes needing a recorded screencast.

requirements.title: A Partner organization
requirements.detail: Only apps in a Partner organization can be distributed to other merchants' stores. Joining is reported as free; App Store registration is a one-time $19.

requirements.title: App Store publication to serve many merchants
requirements.detail: Custom distribution covers one store or one Plus organization. Serving many merchants requires public distribution through the App Store, listed or limited visibility, after review.

requirements.title: Protected customer data approval for public apps
requirements.detail: Public apps need review for any customer data (level 1) and for name, email, phone or address fields (level 2). Custom apps and development-store installs need no review.

requirements.title: Mandatory compliance webhooks
requirements.detail: customers/data_request, customers/redact and shop/redact, with HMAC verification, are required for every App Store app.

requirements.title: Expiring offline tokens for public apps
requirements.detail: Access tokens last 1 hour and refresh tokens up to 90 days. Getting a new token for a store retires the older ones, so a reconnect invalidates the previous connection's token.

requirements.title: Scope changes need merchant approval
requirements.detail: New scopes in a new app version are not applied automatically; merchants must approve them in the Shopify admin.

blockers.title: Rejected for asking for the store URL
blockers.symptom: App review cites requirement 2.3.1 (initiate installation from a Shopify-owned surface).
blockers.fix: Remove any form that asks for the myshopify.com address. Start the install from the App Store listing and start the Composio connection from your App URL using the shop Shopify sends you.

blockers.title: Submission paused for compliance webhooks
blockers.symptom: The app moves to Paused, or the automated checks fail on compliance webhooks.
blockers.fix: Register all three compliance topics, return 401 on an invalid HMAC, and rerun the automated checks.

blockers.title: Customer fields come back null
blockers.symptom: GraphQL returns 200 OK, but name, email, phone or address are null and the errors list says the app is not approved for that field.
blockers.fix: Request protected customer data and the specific fields in the Partner Dashboard, then wait for approval. On a development store, selecting the fields is enough.

blockers.title: Old orders missing or 403 on order calls
blockers.symptom: Only orders from the last 60 days appear, or order tools return 403.
blockers.fix: Request read_all_orders through Shopify's access request, add it to the app version only after approval, then reconnect in Composio with that scope.

blockers.title: 400 error when connecting, or version release fails
blockers.symptom: Composio's connection fails with a Shopify OAuth 400, or releasing a version fails with an app_access validation error on scopes.
blockers.fix: Re-enter the client secret in Composio, and remove any approval-required scope you haven't been approved for yet.

blockers.title: Redirect URL mismatch
blockers.symptom: The install screen errors before the merchant can approve.
blockers.fix: Make the app version's redirect URL identical to the redirect URI in your Composio auth config. Copy it from the Composio dashboard, not from an older article.

blockers.title: Second merchant can't install a custom app
blockers.symptom: The install link only works for the store it was generated for.
blockers.fix: Custom distribution covers one store or one Plus organization. Use public distribution to serve many merchants.

blockers.title: Merchant's staff member can't install
blockers.symptom: The person approving the install can't add apps, or can't approve a paid app.
blockers.fix: The store owner grants 'Manage and install apps and channels' (and 'Approve app charges' for paid apps), or installs it themselves.

blockers.title: Review stuck at 'assigning a reviewer'
blockers.symptom: Weeks pass with no reviewer assigned.
blockers.fix: Wait and don't resubmit. Shopify staff said in May 2026 that about 30 days to assignment was normal. Contact Partner support if well past that.

agentCan: Pick the minimum scopes for the Composio Shopify tools you use
Prepare every value to paste into the Dev Dashboard
Create the Composio auth config through Composio's API once you give it the Client ID and Secret through a secure channel
Build the App URL handler that starts the connection from the shop Shopify passes, the embedded admin page, and the three compliance webhooks
Draft the protected customer data justifications, the listing copy and the reviewer test instructions
Write a shot list for any screencast the reviewer asks for
youMust: Choose the distribution method (it is permanent)
Sign up for the Partner Program and create the app in the Dev Dashboard
Decide how merchants pay, and pay the $19 App Store registration
Declare your data protection practices and submit the protected customer data request
Submit for review, answer the reviewer, and record any screencast they ask for
Approve the first install on your development store to test

unknowns.question: Does Composio request expiring offline tokens (expiring=1) for Shopify and refresh them?
unknowns.whyItMatters: Shopify won't accept non-expiring offline tokens from new public apps on the GraphQL Admin API. If Composio doesn't request expiring tokens, a public app's connections would fail.
unknowns.draftEmail: Hi Composio team, we're using our own public Shopify app with the SHOPIFY toolkit. Shopify requires new public apps to use expiring offline access tokens (expiring=1 on the code exchange, 1-hour access tokens, rotating refresh tokens). Does Composio's Shopify OAuth2 flow request expiring tokens and refresh them automatically? Thanks.

unknowns.question: Can the Shopify subdomain be passed through Composio's API so the merchant never types it?
unknowns.whyItMatters: App Store requirement 2.3.1 forbids asking merchants for their store address, which is what Composio's hosted connect form does.
unknowns.draftEmail: Hi Composio team, Shopify App Store rules require installs to start on Shopify and forbid asking merchants for their myshopify.com address. Can we initiate a Shopify connection through the API with the subdomain prefilled from the shop parameter Shopify passes to our App URL, so the merchant goes straight to the OAuth screen and then back to our app UI? Thanks.

unknowns.question: Is there a Composio-managed Shopify app or not?
unknowns.whyItMatters: The toolkit page says managed OAuth is not available, but its FAQ says the default Shopify OAuth app 'may be under review or expired'.
unknowns.draftEmail: Hi Composio team, your Shopify toolkit page says Composio-managed OAuth is not available, but its FAQ mentions a default Shopify OAuth app that may be under review or expired. Is there a managed Shopify app at all today? Thanks.

unknowns.question: Can you run one custom-distribution app per merchant instead of going public?
unknowns.whyItMatters: It would avoid App Store review for a handful of merchants, but Shopify's revenue share page says apps distributed to multiple merchants must go through the App Store.
unknowns.draftEmail: Hi Shopify Partner team, we build an AI agent that connects to merchants' stores. For a small number of merchants, may we create a separate custom-distribution app for each merchant, or does serving multiple merchants require public distribution through the App Store? Thanks.

unknowns.question: Will Shopify accept an agent app whose tools include Composio's legacy REST actions?
unknowns.whyItMatters: New public apps must use only the GraphQL Admin API, and Composio's toolkit still includes REST compatibility actions.
unknowns.askWhom: Composio support, then Shopify App Review
unknowns.draftEmail: Hi Composio team, Shopify requires new public apps to use only the GraphQL Admin API. Which SHOPIFY toolkit actions call the REST Admin API, so we can exclude them from a public app? Thanks.

unknowns.question: How long does a protected customer data review take today?
unknowns.whyItMatters: Level 2 data (customer names, emails, addresses, phones) gates most order and customer tools in a public app.
unknowns.draftEmail: Hi Shopify Partner team, we plan to request level 2 protected customer data for a public app. What is the current typical review time, and is it part of the App Store review or a separate queue? Thanks.

claims.text: New admin-created custom apps can no longer be created (reported from January 1, 2026); new apps use the Dev Dashboard or Shopify CLI.

sources.title: Shopify: Generate access tokens for admin-created custom apps
sources.quote: You can no longer create new admin-created custom apps.

sources.title: Shopify developer community: Starting January 1, 2026, you will not be able to create new legacy custom apps

claims.text: Store staff need 'Manage and install apps and channels' to install apps, and 'Approve app charges' for paid apps.
Composio's Shopify toolkit page says Composio-managed OAuth is not available and lists OAuth2 and S2S_OAUTH2; its FAQ also says 'The default Shopify OAuth app may be under review or expired.'

sources.title: Composio: Shopify toolkit
sources.quote: Composio-managed OAuth not available

claims.text: Composio's Shopify credentials guide walks through creating a Dev Dashboard app version with App URL, scopes (read/write orders, products, customers, inventory) and redirect URL, copying Client ID and Secret into an OAuth2 auth config with 'Use your own developer credentials', and connecting with the store subdomain; it shows https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback as the redirect URI.

sources.title: Composio: How to create OAuth2 credentials for Shopify
sources.quote: Redirect URI: It must match exactly with your Shopify app configuration

claims.text: Composio's Shopify KB says: use OAuth2 or S2S instead of API-key auth; copy the current callback because older v1/v3 paths can fail; pass only the store name as subdomain; a 400 usually means a wrong client secret or unapproved gated scopes; Composio handles token refresh for custom credentials; 403 on orders can mean missing read_all_orders.

sources.title: Composio KB: Shopify toolkit (last verified Aug 17, 2026)
sources.quote: Older or mistyped v1/v3 callback paths can cause OAuth redirect failures, so copy the current value rather than relying on a hard-coded URL in this article.

claims.text: Joining the Shopify Partner Program is reported to be free.

sources.title: Razorpay Learn: How to become a Shopify Partner (Apr 2025)
sources.quote: Yes, joining the Shopify Partner Program is completely free.

claims.text: Estimate: setup and build durations come from the number of dashboard steps and the App Store requirements list; not timed in a real attempt.
Composio's Shopify toolkit is GraphQL-first but keeps legacy REST compatibility actions, with 407 tools.

sources.title: Composio: Shopify toolkit
sources.quote: This toolkit is GraphQL-first for new Admin API automations while retaining legacy REST compatibility actions for older workflows

claims.text: Shopify recommends building App Store apps with Shopify CLI rather than the Dev Dashboard, which it positions for quick integrations.

sources.title: Shopify: Create apps using the Dev Dashboard
sources.quote: Creating an app for the app store? Build using Shopify CLI instead.

claims.text: The App Store review page requires app URLs without 'Shopify' or 'Example', compliance webhooks, a 1200 x 1200 icon, an emergency contact, a listing, and passing automated checks before submission.

sources.title: Shopify: Submit your app for review
sources.quote: The app icon must be 1200 x 1200 pixels in size and in either JPEG or PNG format.
